why: A stock that rises early and then falls hard shows that sellers are still in control. Changes at the top of a company can make investors unsure about its future, even when its business is strong.

title: S&P 500 and Dow fall into a correction
summary: Stocks dropped sharply on Friday as worries about AI companies spread across the market. The S&P 500 and the Dow ended the week in what experts call a correction, and the Nasdaq gave back all of its gains for 2026. On our list, SPY fell 3.6% and QQQ fell 5.5%.
why: A correction means prices have fallen at least 10% from a recent high. It happens every few years and is a normal part of investing, but it is a sign that investors are nervous.

title: Report says the SEC is looking into NVIDIA's accounting
summary: A news report said the SEC, the U.S. agency that watches over the stock market, is investigating how NVIDIA does its accounting. The report relied on people familiar with the matter, and NVIDIA had not commented. NVIDIA's stock closed down 14% for the day.
why: An investigation is not proof that a company did anything wrong. But investors dislike not knowing, so a stock can fall a lot until the facts are clear.

title: Anthropic's new stock slips and fails to lift AI chip stocks
summary: Many investors hoped Anthropic's big stock market debut would cheer up AI stocks. Instead, Anthropic's shares slid back close to their $83 starting price on Friday. AI chip makers kept falling with them.
why: When a hot new stock fades quickly, it can be a sign that investors are less excited about a whole theme, here AI. Stocks tied to the same theme often move together.

title: Investors move to bonds while the Fed talks tough on inflation
summary: Treasury yields fell on Friday as investors sold stocks and bought government bonds, which are seen as safer. At the same time, Federal Reserve officials, including Governor Lisa Cook, warned that inflation has been too high for too long. Traders still expect the Fed to raise interest rates again next year.
why: When stocks feel scary, many people buy bonds for safety. Higher interest rates can make borrowing more expensive and can weigh on stock prices, so Fed comments matter a lot.

title: Stock futures bounce after Friday's sell-off
summary: Futures tied to the big U.S. stock indexes rose on Sunday evening and Monday morning, after a rough Friday pushed the S&P 500 into a correction. Tech led the move, with Nasdaq 100 futures up about 1.9% in an early snapshot. This is a short trading week because of Thanksgiving.
why: Futures show what traders expect before the market opens. A bounce can feel good, but one green morning does not tell us the drop is over.

title: Reuters: SEC probe of NVIDIA is focused on its accounting
summary: People familiar with the matter told Reuters that SEC enforcement staff are looking at NVIDIA's accounting. It is not clear which practices are being studied; one question is a 2025 change in how the company splits its sales by country. The SEC and NVIDIA did not comment.
why: Investors trust a company's numbers to judge what it is worth. Questions about those numbers can scare buyers, even though an investigation is not proof that anyone did something wrong.

title: Traders see a Fed rate hike in December as very likely
summary: Pricing in the futures market points to about a 95% chance that the Federal Reserve raises its key rate by a quarter point at its December 8 and 9 meeting. That would lift the range to 4.00% to 4.25%. Some Fed officials have even talked about a bigger move if inflation stays high.
why: When the Fed raises rates, loans get more expensive for people and companies. That can slow the economy and often pushes stock prices down, especially for growth companies.

title: Eli Lilly agrees to buy a Huntington's disease startup
summary: Eli Lilly agreed to buy LoQus23 Therapeutics, a young company working on a possible Huntington's disease treatment, in a deal worth up to $725 million. It is Lilly's second purchase this month, after a $1.5 billion deal for Calytrix Bio about a week earlier.
why: Buying small companies is one way a big drug maker fills its pipeline, the list of future medicines. Early stage research is risky, so many of these bets never become products.

title: NVIDIA brings back Jensen Huang as CEO
summary: NVIDIA's board voted unanimously to put Jensen Huang back in charge as president and CEO, and back on the board. He had stepped down on November 12. The board says its internal review will keep going until it is finished.
why: Investors often worry when a company loses its founder or leader. Getting him back removed a big worry, and the stock jumped about 31% in one day.
source: NVIDIA press release filed with the SEC

title: Stocks have their best day since April 2025
summary: The Dow, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq all jumped on Monday, led by NVIDIA and other AI stocks. The rally came right after a painful Friday sell off. Tech heavy stocks gained the most.
why: Big down days are often followed by big up days. Investors who sold in a panic on Friday missed Monday's bounce.

title: Traders still expect a Fed rate hike in December
summary: Short term Treasury yields rose on Monday as stocks bounced. Futures markets still price a very high chance that the Federal Reserve raises its key rate by a quarter point at its December meeting.
why: When the Fed raises rates, borrowing costs more for people and companies. That can slow the economy and often weighs on fast growing stocks.

title: Analyst upgrades NVIDIA as chip stocks rebound
summary: The research firm Bernstein upgraded NVIDIA to Outperform, which means it expects the stock to do better than the market, and kept its $200 price target. Other chip stocks such as AMD and Broadcom also rose as buyers came back after last week's slide.
why: An upgrade is an analyst's opinion, not a promise. It can move a stock for a day, but the company's real results matter more over time.

title: Stock futures slip after Monday's huge bounce
summary: Early on Tuesday, futures for the Dow, the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were lower. Investors were checking whether Monday's big NVIDIA-led rally could last. Some people who made quick gains were selling to lock them in.
why: After a very big up day, it is common for prices to step back a little. Watching the next few days tells us more than one single day does.

title: Huang will answer questions from Congress on December 1
summary: Jensen Huang agreed to sit for interviews with three House committees on December 1, including the committee on China. NVIDIA's top lawyer is set to follow on December 2. Lawmakers want to know about possible national security risks tied to his exit.
why: What he says, and what lawmakers say afterward, could bring new surprises. Surprises, good or bad, can make a stock jump or drop quickly.

title: AI chip stocks pull the market back down
summary: A day after a huge rally, chip stocks fell. NVIDIA dropped about 6%, AMD almost 9% and Broadcom about 4%. The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% and the Nasdaq fell 1.5%, while the Dow rose about 0.9% thanks to stocks like Amgen and Nike.
why: When a stock jumps a lot in one day, some investors sell to lock in their gains. That is called profit-taking. It shows why one great day does not mean the worries are gone.

title: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for about $41 billion
summary: French drug maker Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 per share in cash. That is about 46% more than Insmed's price before news of talks came out. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027 if regulators and shareholders approve it.
why: Big deals like this show that large drug companies are willing to pay a lot for new medicines. That helped lift many health care stocks today, including Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical.

title: Short trading week for Thanksgiving
summary: U.S. stock markets are closed on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving. On Friday, November 27, they close early at 1 p.m. Eastern time.
why: Fewer people trade around holidays. With fewer buyers and sellers, prices can sometimes jump more than usual on small news.

title: Dell reports a record quarter powered by AI servers
summary: After the market closed on Tuesday, Dell said its quarterly revenue was a record $54.9 billion, roughly double a year earlier. It booked $60.2 billion of new AI orders and now has $132.3 billion of AI orders waiting to be filled. Dell also raised its full year forecast and approved up to $25 billion to buy back its own shares.
why: Dell buys chips and cooling gear to build AI servers, so its orders are a clue about demand for companies like NVIDIA, AMD and Vertiv. Strong orders suggest customers are still spending heavily on AI, even after a rough week for chip stocks.

title: Inflation report and other data come out before the open
summary: Because of Thanksgiving, several reports are bunched into Wednesday morning at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time. They include the PCE inflation report, durable goods orders and weekly jobless claims.
why: PCE is the inflation number the Federal Reserve watches most. If prices are rising faster than expected, the Fed may keep interest rates high, and that can weigh on stocks, especially fast growing tech companies.

title: Inflation rose to 3.8% in October
summary: The government's PCE report showed prices were 3.8% higher in October than a year earlier, faster than September's 3.6%. Core prices, which skip food and energy, rose 3.3%. Personal income grew, but spending after inflation slipped a little.
why: This is the inflation measure the Federal Reserve cares about most. Rising inflation makes it more likely the Fed raises interest rates, and higher rates usually put pressure on stock prices.

title: U.S. proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners
summary: The U.S. trade office proposed tariffs of up to 20% on China, the European Union and 12 other economies after a study of factories making more than the world needs. The plan still needs public comments and hearings, so it could not start before January. Certain computer chips and medicines would be left out.
why: Tariffs are taxes on imported goods. They can raise costs for companies and shoppers, so investors react to the news early, even before anything changes.

title: Dow climbs back from a 1,100 point drop
summary: Stocks fell hard in the morning after the inflation and tariff news. By the end of the day the Dow had recovered its whole loss and finished slightly higher. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq still closed a little lower.
why: Big swings inside one day show how fast investor mood can change. It is a reminder that reacting to the first scary headline can be a mistake.

title: NVIDIA slides again as AI stocks stay under pressure
summary: NVIDIA fell for a second day as worries about inflation and borrowing in the AI industry weighed on chip stocks. Questions about its leadership and its board after the CEO's return also stayed in the news. It closed down 3.9% on Wednesday.
why: NVIDIA is one of the biggest companies in the market, so its moves affect index funds like SPY and QQQ too. When one stock is a big part of a fund, its ups and downs spread to the whole fund.

title: Lockheed Martin gets a vote of confidence from an analyst
summary: Lockheed Martin rose on Tuesday after a Mizuho analyst began covering defense companies and named it one of the favored picks. The stock kept rising on Wednesday, up 2.2%.
why: Analysts study companies and share opinions with investors. A positive new opinion can bring in buyers, but analysts can be wrong, so it is just one clue.

title: Markets closed for Thanksgiving, early close Friday
summary: U.S. stock exchanges are closed on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving. They reopen Friday and close early, at 1 p.m. Eastern time. The bond market is also set to close early on Friday.
why: Fewer people trade on short holiday days. With fewer buyers and sellers, prices can move more than usual, even without big news.

title: Nasdaq erases most of a 4.6% drop
summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell as much as 4.6% during Wednesday's session but closed down just 0.62%. The S&P 500 ended at 7,182.78, down 0.25%, and the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Worries about AI stock prices and inflation drove the early selling.
why: A big drop that mostly goes away shows investors are nervous but still buying on dips. It is a good reminder that the closing number does not tell the whole story of a day.

title: Jobless claims rise slightly to 203,000
summary: The number of people filing for unemployment benefits for the first time rose by 1,000 to 203,000 in the week ended November 14. Economists had expected about 197,000. People still getting benefits rose to about 1.76 million.
why: Unemployment claims show how many people are losing jobs. The number is still low, which means most people are keeping their jobs, but a slow rise is worth watching.

title: Retail group expects slightly fewer Thanksgiving weekend shoppers
summary: The National Retail Federation surveyed almost 8,000 adults about their holiday plans. It expects about 182.7 million people to shop from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, around 2% fewer than its forecast a year ago. Black Friday is still the top day, with about 126 million planned shoppers.
why: Spending by regular people is the biggest part of the U.S. economy. Holiday shopping can show whether families feel confident or worried, which affects stores and online sellers like Amazon. Keep in mind this is a survey of plans, not actual sales.

title: Senate committee calls former NVIDIA CEO to testify
summary: The Senate Banking Committee asked Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's founder and former CEO, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify about AI chip sales to China. Huang later agreed to appear. A hearing date had not been confirmed in the latest reports.
why: A public hearing can bring new rules or new headlines about where NVIDIA is allowed to sell its chips. Uncertainty like this can make a stock swing more than usual, even before anything changes.

title: Asian stocks mostly rise before Wall Street reopens
summary: Most stock markets in Asia moved higher on Friday while U.S. markets were still on their Thanksgiving break. Shares tied to artificial intelligence and computer chips led the gains. Investors are also keeping an eye on planned U.S. tariff increases on imports from several trading partners.
why: Markets around the world often move together. A good night in Asia can set a hopeful mood for the U.S. open, but U.S. traders still make up their own minds once trading starts.

title: Half day for U.S. stocks on Black Friday
summary: U.S. stock exchanges reopen Friday after being closed for Thanksgiving. Trading ends early, at 1 p.m. Eastern time. Many traders take the day off, so fewer shares usually change hands.
why: When fewer people are trading, prices can swing more than normal on small amounts of news. A big move on a short day may not mean much for the long run.

title: Online holiday spending is up 9.1% so far
summary: Adobe says U.S. shoppers spent $82.5 billion online from November 1 to 22, up 9.1% from a year earlier. It expects about $12.9 billion in online sales on Black Friday. The Black Friday figure is a forecast, and the data does not include shopping in stores.
why: Spending by regular people is the biggest part of the U.S. economy. When shoppers keep buying, companies like Amazon can earn more. Strong spending can also keep prices rising, which matters for interest rates.

title: NVIDIA's CEO will face a Senate hearing on December 3
summary: Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify in public before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3. The hearing is about U.S. rules that limit selling advanced chips to other countries. He is also set to meet privately with House committees on December 1.
why: Government rules can change where a company is allowed to sell its products. If lawmakers push for tighter limits, chip companies could sell less abroad, so investors will listen closely.

title: Stocks finish a short holiday week with a big gain
summary: U.S. stocks climbed in the half day session after Thanksgiving. The Dow rose about 590 points, or about 1.2%, the S&P 500 gained about 1.6% and the Nasdaq added about 2.3%. Tech and chip companies led the way, and the Nasdaq ended the week with one of its best weekly gains in a long time.
why: A strong week after a big drop shows how fast the mood of the market can change. It is a good reminder not to panic on bad days, and also not to get too excited on great days.

title: Chip and memory stocks lead the bounce
summary: Companies that make computer chips and memory had some of the biggest gains of the day. On our list, AMD rose 4.6%, Broadcom 3.8%, TSMC 3.2% and Vertiv 3.1%. Investors bought back into AI related shares after the holiday break.
why: These companies sell the parts that power artificial intelligence. Their stocks tend to rise faster on good days and fall faster on bad days, which is why our page gives them higher risk scores.

title: Anthropic's new stock climbs back above its IPO price
summary: Shares of Anthropic, the AI company that started trading on the stock market last week, rose about 10% today. That pushed the price above $90, higher than the $83 price set for its IPO. Its first days of trading had been bumpy.
why: An IPO is when a company sells shares to the public for the first time. Amazon and Alphabet have both invested in Anthropic, so how its stock does can affect how investors feel about AI and about those two companies.

title: NVIDIA paused sales of some approved AI chips to China
summary: On its earnings call, NVIDIA said it had stopped shipping some Hopper family AI chips to China, even though the U.S. had allowed those sales. The company sold about $2.4 billion of these licensed chips to China last quarter. It did not say why it stopped or whether the pause is permanent.
why: China is a big market. When a company stops selling there, future sales could be lower. NVIDIA rose much less than other chip stocks today, and its CEO faces questions from Congress next week, so this story is worth following.
